title: Animal Life Cycles
seo_title: Primary 2 Basic Science: Animal Life Cycles Worksheets (NERDC)
standard_code: Primary 2 Basic Science: Living and Non-Living Things
standard_text: Animals go through life cycles: birth or hatching, growth, adulthood, reproduction and death. Some animals look like their parents when young; others, such as frogs and butterflies, change form (metamorphosis). (summary of the Basic Science curriculum, Primary 2, theme: Living and Non-Living Things)
meta_desc: Free Primary 2 Basic Science worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: Living and Non-Living Things): life cycles, babies and parents, growing up, metamorphosis and how parents care for their young. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: All animals are born, grow, reproduce and die.
key_sub: Butterflies and frogs change shape as they grow.
body_html:
How to think about it

A life cycle is the series of stages in an animal's life. A chicken hatches from an egg, grows into a chick, then an adult hen that lays eggs.

Some animals change form: a butterfly goes from egg to larva (caterpillar) to pupa to adult; a frog goes from egg to tadpole to froglet to adult. Many animal parents protect and feed their young.

Example

Stages of a butterfly?

Four stages

Answer: egg → larva → pupa → adult

Example

Does a puppy look like its parents?

Mammals

Answer: yes, a smaller version

Common mistakes

  • Thinking caterpillars and butterflies are different animals.
  • Thinking a tadpole is a fish.
  • Thinking all animals lay eggs.
